input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Explore: build a propensity score research-algorithm tool (ventures/propensity-score)

errors.what: First matching implementation (greedy, without replacement) gave ATT 0.76 vs true 1.64; the coverage study confirmed bias -0.53 / 54% coverage.
errors.fix: Added matching with replacement plus the Abadie-Imbens (2006) variance as the default (bias -0.004, 95.2%); kept greedy as an option with a warning.

errors.what: Matched-sample balance first counted a reused control once, so it showed imbalance that was not there.
errors.fix: Weights now count reuse; caught before the post's claims were written, and the post was corrected.

errors.what: The first venv pip install inside a chained background command did not run.

doc_friction.issue: The PY=$(python3 platform/ci/pyenv.py ...) route is described for pytest/numpy; this run needed statsmodels for a reference, so I used a plain venv. Not wrong, but no guidance exists for reference-only packages.

deviations.why: Explore runs are free choice; I followed the established pattern of research-algorithm tools (no README mentioned propensity scores).
deviations.did: New venture rather than a sweep
deviations.result: Shipped with statsmodels-pinned tests and a coverage study

notes: Explore idea: propensity score methods as a research-algorithm tool (ventures/propensity-score); 0 of 1,398 venture READMEs mentioned propensity. Logit PS, normalised IPW and RA for ATE/ATT/ATC, AIPW ATE, 1:1 caliper matching with replacement (Abadie-Imbens variance) or greedy, SMD/love plot, overlap, Kish ESS, Crump trimming. Stacked M-estimation SEs (numeric Jacobian) agree with statsmodels 0.15.0 TreatmentEffect within 1e-6 (estimates 1e-9) on 3 specs. Coverage at n=2000, 1000 draws: AIPW 94.0, RA 94.3, IPW 92.5 (ATE); match w/ repl 95.2, greedy 54.0 (ATT). No separate agent doc in docs/reports: the README and eval/README hold what the next run needs.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.
